summary: Sustained 5xx increase after automated TLS key rollover caused connection re-handshake storm and upstream runtime restarts
description:
Issue summary: After an automated TLS key rollover triggered by the keystore rotation job at ~2026-03-13T22:10Z, we observed a progressive increase in 5xx responses from the API gateway over ~30 minutes. API gateway metrics show accept-queue growth and elevated connection reset rates; upstream serving runtimes experienced frequent SIGTERM/restart cycles and GPU preemption events.

Impact: Customer-facing API calls for AcmeAI (dedicated) experienced ~8-12% 5xx rate across text-generation and embeddings endpoints in us-east for ~45 minutes. Latency P95 increased from ~120ms to ~650ms. Some long-lived streaming sessions dropped mid-response.

Environment: prod | us-east. Dedicated pool (tenant: acmeai-dedicated-01). Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream, /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings/upload.

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Keystore rotation job (automated) completed key swap at 2026-03-13T22:10Z.
2) API gateway TLS sessions started failing early resumption checks; logs show ECDHE handshake retries and late session cache misses.
3) Client reconnects + hedged retries caused accept-queue length to grow on the gateway; backpressure propagated to the runtime proxy layer.
4) Serving runtimes began to report increased GPU preemption and graceful-shutdown cycles when prefetched KV operations hit timeouts.
5) Healthchecks from autoscaler flagged unstable pods, causing flapping and more connection churn.

Observed logs & metrics (high-level):
- apigw TLS handshake fail rate spike @22:11: ~1200 failures/min (see apigw-tls-handshake-22-11.png in runbook).
- apigw accept_queue_length: steady 500->4200 over 15m.
- runtime watchdog restarts: +320 restarts in 30m; nvml driver logs show preemption messages.
- client retry rate: 3x baseline due to identity resumption failure.
- error responses returned: 502 for upstream termination, 504 for downstream timeouts, occasional 503 during accept queue saturation.

Immediate customer visible message: We proactively communicated via support channel that we detected an elevated error rate and were investigating.
investigation_notes:
- Hypothesis A: Keystore rotation caused session-resumption cache misses, clients performed full TLS handshakes resulting in CPU + accept queue pressure on API gateway.
- Hypothesis B: Hedged retries from SDKs amplified the connection churn, causing upstream runtime proxy to hit fd limits and trigger graceful restarts.
- Hypothesis C: Autoscaler reacted to transient latency by killing/recreating pods, creating further cold starts and GPU preemption.

What we've checked so far:
- Confirmed rotation job timeline and keys deployed successfully; keystore service logs show ephemeral increase in latency around 22:10.
- Captured apigw TLS logs (filtered) showing session cache eviction errors and clients falling back to full ECDHE.
- Runtime logs show series of SIGTERM followed by restart (stack traces attached in internal runbook).
- System-level: node-level NVMe iowait remained normal; GPU memory logs show fragmentation but not steady OOMs.

Investigative actions in flight:
- Throttled incoming new TLS handshakes at the apigw layer (connection accept-smoothing) to reduce accept-queue growth.
- Temporarily disabled hedged-retry behavior for acmeai tenant via edge config to cut client-side amplification.
- Coordinated with infra to pause autoscaler aggressive downscale for affected nodepool to avoid scale churn.
- Replaying metrics to confirm that session resumption policy (ticket lifetime) needs tuning during rollover.

2026-03-13 23:05 - SRE (Nadia): Paused autoscaler downscale for nodepool; runtime restarts decreased but not eliminated. Suggest keystore hotfix to avoid full-session rebuilds during rotations.

resolution:
Mitigation applied: accept-smoothing on apigw and temporary hedged-retry suppression reduced immediate pressure; autoscaler pause prevented additional pod churn. Longer-term fix planned: keystore hotpatch to perform staged ticket rollout + session-ticket warmup, and a runtime proxy improvement to handle bursty TLS full-handshakes without triggering restarts.

Follow-ups / action items:
- CH-1: Deploy keystore staging hotfix that staggers ticket invalidation (owner: infra/keystore).
- CH-2: Add apigw rate-limiter knob to limit new TLS full-handshakes per tenant (owner: edge).
- CH-3: Improve autoscaler hysteresis for dedicated pools to avoid scale churn during short transient latency events (owner: scheduler).
- CH-4: Post-incident review and update TLS key rotation runbook; include checklist to monitor accept-queue and session-resumption hit-rate before eviction (owner: SRE).

Status: Mitigations in place, fixes scheduled. Monitoring shows error-rate back to ~1% and P95 latency decreasing.
